primitives.name: Ordinal Team Ranking Sequence
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_i': 'ordinal rank of team i', 'R_i': 'rating of team i'}
primitives.assumptions: Higher ordinal rank corresponds to higher performance; ties allowed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S_i = S_j and R_i = R_j, ranking ambiguity occurs.

layer2.mapping: GSE's state transition graph encodes team rankings as nodes with edge weights representing expected performance differentials.

primitives.name: Rating Variance Deviation
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'σ_R': 'standard deviation of team ratings', 'ΔR_i': "deviation of team i's rating from mean"}
primitives.assumptions: Deviation reflects volatility in team form; normal distribution assumed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When σ_R exceeds threshold, model instability detected.

layer2.mapping: GSI's uncertainty quantifier computes confidence intervals around R_i using ΔR_i; GSE applies this to adjust strategic planning parameters.
layer2.telemetry: Variance in predicted vs actual game results

reasoning_traces.think:
The PowerRankings system operates as a structured ordinal regression framework where each team is assigned a scalar rating that reflects its relative strength. These ratings are derived from historical performance data and serve as inputs to a probabilistic model. The ordinal nature implies a strict ordering which enables dualities such as dominance relationships between teams. Failure modes include overfitting due to small sample sizes or temporal shifts in team form not captured by static ratings. The system assumes stationarity of team capabilities and ignores external factors like injuries or coaching changes unless encoded in the rating.
